etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French asseurer (Modern French assurer), from Latin ad- + securus (“secure”). Cognate with Spanish asegurar. Doublet of assecure.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make sure and secure; ensure.
(transitive, followed by that or of) To give (someone) confidence in the trustworthiness of (something).

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book II, Canto II”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: That as a law for euer should endure; / Which to obserue in word of knights they did assure.
